title: Quasi-finiteness at a prime passes along a square with surjective tensor map
statement: Let $R\to S$, $R\to R'$, $R'\to S'$ and $S\to S'$ be homomorphisms of commutative rings with $R\to S\to S'$ equal to $R\to R'\to S'$. Assume that $R\to S$ is of finite type [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra] and that $S'$ is generated as a ring by the images of $S$ and of $R'$ in the sense that every element of $S'$ is a finite sum $\sum_i \sigma_i\rho_i$ with $\sigma_i$ in the image of $S$ and $\rho_i$ in the image of $R'$ (equivalently, the map $S\otimes_RR'\to S'$, $s\otimes r'\mapsto \sigma\rho$, is surjective); then $R'\to S'$ is of finite type. Let $\mathfrak q'\subset S'$ be a prime ideal, and let $\mathfrak q\subset S$, $\mathfrak p'\subset R'$ be its inverse images. If $R\to S$ is quasi-finite at $\mathfrak q$ [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime], then $R'\to S'$ is quasi-finite at $\mathfrak q'$.

proof.text: Construct a finite set of R'-algebra generators by taking images of finite R-algebra generators of S. Induction on algebra adjoin and the two scalar-tower identities show that the image of S lies in their adjoin. The finite-sum hypothesis then puts every element of S' in that adjoin.

Use PrimeSpectrum.preimageHomeomorphFiber and Algebra.quasiFiniteAt_iff_isOpen_singleton_fiber to convert the source isolated fibre point to Mathlib QuasiFiniteAt. The homeomorphism identifies the canonical point used in IsQuasiFiniteAtPrime with the corresponding point in the topological fibre.

Construct f : R' tensor_R S -> S' as an R'-algebra homomorphism with Algebra.TensorProduct.lift. For each finite-sum presentation of x, the sum of pure tensors r_i tensor s_i maps to x, so f is surjective. Contract q' to Q along f; computing f on includeRight proves Q contracts to q in S.

Apply the proved Mathlib theorem Algebra.QuasiFiniteAt.baseChange at Q, then Algebra.QuasiFiniteAt.of_surjectiveOnStalks along f, using RingHom.surjectiveOnStalks_of_surjective. These are direct applications of Mathlib/RingTheory/QuasiFinite/Basic.lean and introduce no project proof holes.

Apply Algebra.quasiFiniteAt_iff_isOpen_singleton_fiber to q' and transport openness through PrimeSpectrum.preimageHomeomorphFiber over R'. Its image of the singleton is exactly the canonical fibre-ring point in IsQuasiFiniteAtPrime, proving the original conclusion with the constructed finite-type instance.
